python-fundamentals.longDescription: Start from zero and build real, working software. This course walks through Python's core syntax — variables, loops, functions, and file handling — entirely through the lens of one project: a budget tracker you'll actually be able to use afterwards.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A command line budget tracker that logs income and expenses to a file and reports monthly totals.

learnPoints: Write and structure Python scripts with functions
Work with lists, dictionaries, and loops confidently
Read from and write to files to persist data
Handle user input and basic errors gracefully

curriculum.title: Module 3: Final Project — The Budget Tracker

requirements: Basic computer literacy and ability to install software.
No prior coding experience required — we start from absolute basics.
A Mac, PC, or Linux machine with an internet connection.

instructor.bio: Nomvula is a Senior Data Scientist with over 8 years of experience building predictive models and data infrastructure for top financial institutions. She's passionate about breaking down complex concepts into practical, hands on lessons.

reviews.name: James D.
reviews.quote: Incredibly structured. I went from knowing zero Python to building my own scripts in just a few weeks.

reviews.name: Sarah T.
reviews.quote: The pacing is rigorous but completely accessible for beginners. Highly recommend.

reviews.name: Michael K.
reviews.quote: No fluff, just solid foundational skills. The pacing is rigorous but completely accessible for beginners.

reviews.name: Aisha R.
reviews.quote: Great first Python course. Would have liked a bit more on error handling edge cases.

python-automation.longDescription: Stop doing repetitive file cleanup by hand. This course teaches practical automation with Python's standard library by having you build a tool that sorts, renames, and organizes files on demand.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A file organizer script that automatically sorts a messy downloads folder by file type and date.

learnPoints: Automate file and folder operations with Python
Work confidently with paths, globs, and the OS module
Schedule and trigger scripts to run automatically
Package a script so it's easy to reuse

lessons.title: Why automate? Real world use cases

requirements: Comfortable with basic Python syntax (variables, loops, functions).
A Mac, PC, or Linux machine with Python installed.
A folder of test files to practice organizing (we provide samples too).

instructor.bio: Reece is a backend engineer who has spent years building internal tooling to remove repetitive work from engineering teams. He teaches automation the way he wishes it was taught to him: through real, messy problems.

reviews.name: Karabo M.
reviews.quote: Immediately useful. I automated my own downloads folder the same day.

reviews.name: Liam P.
reviews.quote: Great practical content, would love a follow up on more advanced scheduling.

reviews.name: Sipho D.
reviews.quote: Turned a repetitive weekly chore into a five minute script. Exactly what I needed.

reviews.name: Grace M.
reviews.quote: Solid course, the scheduling section could use one more real example.

cpp-fundamentals.longDescription: Understand what's really happening under the hood. This course covers memory management, pointers, and object-oriented basics in C++ by having you design and build a working inventory management system.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A console based inventory system with classes for products, stock levels, and simple reporting.

learnPoints: Understand pointers, references, and memory management
Design classes and objects with proper encapsulation
Work with the Standard Template Library (STL)
Structure a multi file C++ project
requirements: Basic programming familiarity in any language is helpful but not required.
A Mac, PC, or Linux machine able to run a C++ compiler.
Willingness to work with the command line.

instructor.bio: Amara is a systems engineer with a background in performance critical software. She has spent her career close to the metal and enjoys demystifying memory management for newer developers.

reviews.name: Tumi S.
reviews.quote: Finally understood pointers properly after years of confusion. Well explained.

reviews.name: Michael K.
reviews.quote: Solid foundational course, the inventory project ties it all together nicely.

reviews.name: Neo T.
reviews.quote: The inventory project made pointers finally make sense in a practical context.

reviews.name: Chris L.
reviews.quote: Thorough and well paced, good for anyone coming from a higher level language.

postgresql-essentials.longDescription: Learn relational database design the practical way: by modeling, querying, and optimizing a real bookstore schema from scratch, covering everything from table design to indexing.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A working bookstore database with authors, books, orders, and optimized queries for common lookups.

learnPoints: Design normalized relational schemas
Write joins, subqueries, and aggregate queries
Use indexes to speed up slow queries
Model real world relationships between tables
requirements: No prior database experience required.
PostgreSQL installed locally (setup guide included).
Basic comfort with the command line is helpful.

instructor.bio: Dylan is a backend engineer who has designed data models for products handling millions of records. He believes good schema design prevents most of the bugs teams fight later.

reviews.name: Naledi V.
reviews.quote: Clear, practical, and the bookstore project made everything click.

reviews.name: Andre F.
reviews.quote: Great intro to indexing — wish it went a little deeper on optimization.

reviews.name: Zola N.
reviews.quote: The bookstore project ties every concept together really well. Highly recommend.

reviews.name: Peter H.
reviews.quote: Great schema design fundamentals, wish there was a module on backups too.

java-fundamentals.longDescription: Build a real application while learning Java's core concepts: classes, interfaces, and collections, all in service of a working library management system you design from the ground up.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A library management app that tracks books, members, and loans using core Java collections.

learnPoints: Design classes, interfaces, and inheritance hierarchies
Use Java's collections framework effectively
Handle exceptions and validate input safely
Structure a small multi class application
requirements: No prior Java experience required.
A Mac, PC, or Linux machine with the JDK installed (setup guide included).
Basic problem solving mindset — we'll teach the syntax.

instructor.bio: Priya is a software engineer who has led backend teams building enterprise Java systems. She focuses on teaching Java the way it's actually used in production, not just in theory.

reviews.name: Bongani Z.
reviews.quote: Really well paced. The library project pulled together everything from earlier modules.

typescript-for-js-devs.longDescription: Already know JavaScript? This course adds TypeScript's type system on top of skills you already have, by rebuilding a familiar todo app as a fully type safe application.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A type safe todo app rebuilt from JavaScript, using interfaces and generics throughout.

learnPoints: Add static types to existing JavaScript code
Design interfaces and type aliases
Use generics to write reusable, type safe functions
Catch bugs at compile time instead of runtime
requirements: Solid working knowledge of JavaScript (ES6+).
Node.js installed locally.
Familiarity with basic frontend concepts is helpful.

instructor.bio: Kagiso is a frontend engineer who migrated several production JavaScript codebases to TypeScript. He teaches the migration mindset, not just the syntax.

reviews.name: Zanele P.
reviews.quote: Exactly what I needed as a JS dev — no fluff, straight into practical typing.

html-css-foundations.longDescription: Learn the building blocks of the web from scratch: semantic HTML, layout with CSS, and responsive design, all while building and styling your own portfolio site.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A fully responsive personal portfolio site, built and styled from a blank page.

learnPoints: Write clean, semantic HTML markup
Layout pages confidently with Flexbox and Grid
Build responsive designs that work on any screen
Style a real site from scratch, without a framework
requirements: No prior coding experience required — we start from absolute basics.
A Mac, PC, or Linux machine with a text editor and browser.
No design experience needed.

instructor.bio: Sipho is a frontend developer and former bootcamp instructor who specializes in teaching complete beginners. He believes anyone can learn to build for the web with the right first course.

reviews.name: Marco B.

reactjs-fundamentals.longDescription: Learn modern React by building something real: a movie search app that talks to a live API, covering components, hooks, and state management along the way.

projectFocus.title: What you'll build
projectFocus.description: A movie search app that queries a live API and manages loading, error, and result states.

learnPoints: Build and compose functional components
Manage state and side effects with hooks
Fetch and display data from a live API
Handle loading and error states gracefully
requirements: Solid working knowledge of JavaScript (ES6+).
Node.js installed locally.
No prior React experience required.

instructor.bio: Chloe is a frontend engineer who has built and maintained production React applications for several years. She focuses on teaching patterns that hold up in real codebases, not just tutorials.

reviews.quote: Building against a real API from lesson one made everything click faster.
